name: Light–籁 cross-modal forced-choice study
primary_question: Does the spoken form /laɪ/ or /laɪt/ increase selection of bright/light-related stimuli relative to matched control forms?

tasks: forced choice between brightness-matched visual pairs after hearing target or control forms
semantic association ratings for LIGHT versus SOUND/MUSIC concepts

primary_outcome: Difference in probability of choosing the bright/light-associated stimulus between target and matched-control conditions.
disconfirmation_criteria: no reliable target-control difference with an equivalence bound fixed before collection
